To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the effort by lead users in each stage of innovation problem solving is, in varying degree, associated with software quality, development productivity, and software popularity; 2) front loading the problem-solving process is associated with increased software quality but decreased development process productivity; and 3) engaging users in either problem-solving stage is always negatively associated with productivity.
the problem solving view of new product innovation is a useful framework to study user-led innovation.
effort in user-led problem solving is associated with better product quality, and that front loading the problem-solving process yields better software.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of LUs in problem solving and how this role impacts software development performance.
how to best engage users in the innovation process and the impact on performance.
the role of users in software development, in particular with the role of LUs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
user-led problem solving is beneficial to the product quality but negatively impacts the productivity of the process.

engaging lead users (Lus) in problem detection and problem removal stages is associated with higher code quality, while front loading the problem analysis stage is associated with higher quality but lower productivity.
engaging LUs in problem solving is beneficial for the software's quality, but not for its development productivity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

engaging users in either problem analysis or problem removal stage negatively impacts productivity, while engaging users in problem analysis is related with higher product quality and front loading the problem-solving process yields better software.
engaging users in the problem solving process of new product development is associated with increased quality but reduced productivity.
the more effort users put into the problem solving process, the more they help in the creation of a high quality product.
The main takeaway from our work is that
user participation in software innovation can be beneficial, but only if it is carefully managed and targeted to specific problem-solving stages.

user participation in software product development is associated with better product quality and popularity, and with increased development productivity, if the user participation occurs early in the problem solving process, and if the user input is directed to the problem analysis stage.
the problem-solving view of innovation provides a new perspective to understand the role of lead users in software development.
